title: Fantastic App so far
body:
As someone with ADHD, I've always needed music to focus. I've spent over a decade defaulting to rap, hip-hop, and EDM because they're what I liked, not what my brain needed. These genres keep my nervous system elevated. I thought I was focused (sorry, I meant to say I thought that was focus). Brain.FM changed that two weeks in, and I'm using it to wind down before bed, calm down after the gym, and read effortlessly without distraction for the first time in my entire life. I have a tool designed for what I actually need instead of what just overstimulates me. This is an app I didn't know I was missing. Thank you.

Only suggestion I would add to make this a 5 star would be to add some sort of community driven factor for neurodivergent fellows who want to collaborate together or to have some sort of other resources to help them with their struggles (ie, studying methods, at-home organization structuring, focus strategies)

title: Good concept, frustrating UI
body:
As someone with ADHD I find Brain.fm useful, especially to help me sleep.

The app is pretty enough, but very frustrating and difficult to use. There are two core issues the team needs to address.

1. When you select a category like deep sleep, it automatically chooses a track. There is no way to choose, it just starts playing. The only way I can find what I want is to click details and see what the track is, and then use the filters to try and narrow down the choices. I want deep sleep and I prefer low brightness. But The cannot set that filter and see the tracks that match my criteria and choose one. I don’t know if 0, 1, 3, or 10 tracks match what I want, it just automatically picks one to play with no information, no feedback, and no choice. For sleeping I like beach, wind, water, and night sounds, but there is no way to filter for those tracks that are beach or wind and low brightness. Even if there was, it just plays one with no choice or feedback. The only way to find tracks I like is to keep twiddling the filters and then listen and click details to see the neural effect, brightness, and sound type. Then keep blindly doing that over and over until I stumble into a track I like.

2. There needs to be a way to set up a play list so that it’s not just one track playing for 8 hours. It can get repetitive. There is an end to each track and you can hear when it ends and restarts. What I need is the ability to select multiple tracks and have it play one, then the next, then the next etc. I want to be able to set how long before it changes, say 90 minutes, and have it automatically move through the playlist and repeat as needed with the option to shuffle. I need to be able to choose deep sleep racks for the first part of the night and sleep and wake for the later stages, with something to help me wake up at the end.

It’s also frustrating that every time there is a notification of new tracks since I started a few months ago, there have been no new sleep tracks.  There is only one guided sleep track, and the only way to find that out is to keep pressing guided sleep and always getting that one track. There needs to be more guided sleep options with different voices, different talk tracks, etc.

I am hoping the team can make the app easier to use and work on more sleep content.

One more thing. I use this primarily for slee

title: generally pretty good
body:
this app is honestly mostly as described! if you don’t wanna spend time looking for playlists that will help you focus this is perfect for you!

i only gave it 3 stars however for a couple of reasons:

1. they don’t allow you to set custom times, for example if i know i have exactly 45 minutes before i need to start getting ready for something, then i have to either settle for 30 or an hour there is no option to customize.

2. the price is steep for what it is, and the reality is (at least for myself, as someone with ADHD) it doesn’t do a whole lot more than a good lofi playlist. the main pull is the “neural effect” which admittedly is very nice! (it’s essentially modulating of sounds within the song at different speeds from ear to ear) but that just doesn’t feel enough to give me the value i need at the price point they’re asking for.

3. i was only able to find one study about the benefits of the modulation (neural effect) and it only specified that it benefitted people with ADHD, which generally i assume a lot of people using this app will not have ADHD. which to me kind of defeats the purpose of an all encompassing focus/relaxation app if the focus part is designated to a very specific aspect of neurodiversity. this (in my opinion) also harms the “backed by science” claim they make, since a majority of the studies they link to are sponsored/paid for by them. which again, possibly causes conflict of interest.

i think this app has some benefits and could be useful for people who don’t care to search for a good lofi playlist on spotify, but for most people this app is over glorified and not worth the money. for the same amount you could get access to spotify’s countless hours of user generated playlists, & even create your own playlists. the only thing you’ll miss out on is the modulation, which again, only seems to benefit a small group of listeners.

2 hr tracks, my wallet is open

author: Canuckfan1969

title: A new daily necessity
body:
I almost never write reviews, but this app is worth paying attention to. I originally bought this app to study in a noisy environment and it has worked well in that task. But what has been the most amazing is how it can affect alertness and sleep. 
I work nights... being alert and awake during this time has always been hard. I work in an environment that allows me to wear earbuds, so I listen to this app while working. It keeps me awake and alert! I don't depend on coffee to get me through my shift when using this app. I am truly amazed...
Also for sleep, when playing the sleep sounds in the background my sleep has never been deeper. I have often had a hard time sleeping in general because of shift work. But this app keeps me asleep. I wake up and feel like I have been in a deep sleep that has settled into my chest. 
The science behind what they have done here works. I am truly impressed and feel I will be a lifetime user. Highly recommended.

title: Score, in the bag!! I like it!
body:
Yeah, this stuff is great. It fills that hole of a sound enhancing app that's not binaural beats! I love the stereo effects. It really melds and mixes with my drifting thoughts like a dance. The energy is positive here and grooms me to sleep nicely. Sleep!! That's not it! Pop focus on and I wake up energized!! Helps me set up for the day too! I downloaded some offline focus to try on my long commute to work. This is another place to set my day's intention and these tracks can help me do that. Oh yeah, Brain.fm you're welcome to come along!! Make yourself at home!

Oh just a tip, I use air tube headphones. These wrap up around the ear and use acoustic tubes to transmit sound, like a doctor's stethoscope. They are super soft and light, great for sleeping. Mine were less then $10 CAD on Ama-zon
